# schema.org First, Custom Vocabulary as Fallback

**Decision.** Describe every entity with **schema.org** terms wherever schema.org has one, and reach
for the project's own `mc:` vocabulary **only** where it does not.

**Date.** 2026-07-09, lab 6 of `Information-Systems-Modelling`.

## The rule, stated and then enforced by code

> "schema.org covers most of the domain. Where it does **not**, the custom `mc:` vocabulary fills the
> gap (the \"missing classes/properties\" case the brief asks about). The renderer applies this rule
> programmatically."
> — Information-Systems-Modelling/lab6/README.md, 2026-07-09

The last sentence is what separates this from a style preference. RDFa wiring sets
`<html vocab="https://schema.org/" prefix="mc: … mcr: …">` once, so a **bare term is schema.org by
default** and a custom term must be explicitly prefixed. Reaching for `mc:` costs six extra
characters and shows up in review; using schema.org is the path of least resistance. The default is
the policy.

Types combine both rather than choosing — `typeof="CreativeWork mc:DroneBuild"` — so a generic
consumer sees a `CreativeWork` and a domain-aware one sees a drone build.

## Where the fallback was actually needed

The mapping table is the decision's evidence: nine domain entities, and only **three** have no
schema.org equivalent at all.

| Covered by schema.org | Falls back to `mc:` |
|---|---|
| Build → `CreativeWork`; votes → `interactionStatistic`/`InteractionCounter`; listing → `Product` + `Offer`; member → `Person`; test run → `Event` + `Place` + `PostalAddress`; club → `Organization` | **Flight log** (`mc:FlightLog`, `mc:flightAltitude`, `mc:pilotLicenseId`) · **Telemetry** (`mc:TelemetryRecord`, `mc:topSpeed`, `mc:crashCount`) · **Reputation** (`mc:ReputationRecord`, four score properties) |

Those three are exactly the parts of the domain a general-purpose web vocabulary has no reason to
model. That the fallback set is *small and principled* is the argument the decision makes.

The `mc:` terms are not invented here — they come from the TBox built in lab 5, so the same
vocabulary serves the reasoner and the published pages. See [[ontology-modelling-tbox-abox]].

## The rejected alternatives

- **Model everything in `mc:`.** Internally consistent, and invisible to every consumer on the web —
  a search engine reading `mc:MarketplaceListing` learns nothing. Rejected.
- **Force everything into schema.org.** Would mean modelling a flight log as a generic
  `CreativeWork` with untyped `additionalProperty` bags, losing the structure lab 5 built.
- **Maintain the mapping by hand in a comment.** Rejected explicitly, and replaced by
  `src/rdf/vocabmap.js`, which **walks the JSON-LD graph** of each page and reports which schema.org
  and which `mc:` terms it actually contains — flagging nodes typed *only* with `mc:` classes as
  custom-only sub-graphs. A hand-written list would go stale the first time the data changed. That is
  [[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]] and [[single-source-of-truth-generators]] applied to
  metadata about metadata.

## Cost, stated in the repo

Custom terms are not understood by third-party validators. `lab6/README.md` records the consequence
rather than hiding it: custom `mc:` properties surface in structured-data testing tools as
"recognised-but-unknown extras (expected — not schema.org terms)". Naming the expected warning is
what stops a future reader from treating it as a defect.
